summary: Nicolaas van Wijk (1880–1942) was a linguist who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1898–1902) and Moscow State University (~1903–1904). He held a post at Leiden University in 1913.
Nicolas Morrissey works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Gregory Schopen (attested 2004) and held a post at the University of Georgia.

Nicolas Revire is a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology. He studied at Silpakorn University (2012–2013), under doctoral supervisors Claudine Bautze-Picron and Peter Skilling, and held a post at Thammasat University (attested 2016).
Nicolas Sihlé is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Anthropology at the University of Virginia (attested 2010).

Nicolas Tournadre (born 1959) is a linguist and Tibetologist who completed a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Claude Hagège. He held positions at INALCO (~1995–2004), University of Provence (~2004–2011), and Aix-Marseille University (~2012).
Nicole Baden (born 1981) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Richard Baker and succeeded him in 2024.

Nicole Vandier-Nicolas (1906–1987) was a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She taught Chinese art at the École du Louvre and served as professor of Chinese civilization at INALCO (~1966–1976).

Niels Ludvig Westergaard (1815–1878) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Copenhagen, Bonn (under Christian Lassen), Paris, and Oxford. He spent his career at the University of Copenhagen as Lektor (1844), professor (1850), and Rektor (1867–1868).
Nigel Allan specializes in history and archaeology. He succeeded Marianne Winder as Curator of Oriental Books and Manuscripts at the Wellcome Institute for the History of Medicine (attested 1993).

Niharranjan Ray (1903–1981) was an Indologist and historian who completed a doctorate at Leiden University (~1935–1936). He was Bageswari Professor of Fine Arts at the University of Calcutta (1946–1965) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1965–1970).

Nika Jovic is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Vienna (attested 2010), where she was supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes, and was taught by Géza Bethlenfalvy (2007–2008).

Nikolai Solmsdorf is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard (attested 2013). He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2013).

Nikolai Trubetzkoy (1890–1938) was a linguist who studied at Moscow University (~1908–1913) and under August Leskien (~1913–1914). He held posts at Sofia University (~1920–1922) and the University of Vienna (~1922–1938).

Nile Green (born 1972) is a historian of religion and Indology. He held a post at the University of Manchester (~2005–2007) before joining the University of California, Los Angeles in ~2007 as a history professor.

Nina Mirnig is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2020) and as Deputy Head at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Ninian Smart (1927–2001) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Oxford and Yale. He served as Foundation Professor of Religious Studies at Lancaster University (1967–1982) and as professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1976–1998).

Nira Wickramasinghe (born 1964) is a scholar of history and Indology who studied at the University of Paris (~1981–1984) and the University of Oxford (~1985–1989). She became Professor of Modern South Asian Studies at Leiden University (~2010).

Nirajan Kafle is an Indologist who completed his doctorate at Leiden University (-2015) under Peter C. Bisschop. He held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2019) and Leiden University (attested 2021).

Niranjan Prasad Chakravarti (1893–1956) was an Indologist and archaeologist who earned a PhD at Cambridge. He had an extensive career with the Archaeological Survey of India, culminating as Director General of Archaeology in India (1948–1950).

Niras Ruangsan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2015) under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
